campbell.title: Campbell City Council — July 7, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered a new interim ordinance related to state Senate legislation, along with public hearings on revoking the business license and tobacco retailer permits for two local shops, California Cigar and Hayes Smoke Shop. The council also considered authorizing a grant application for public works funding and approving consultant service agreements.
keyTopics: Interim ordinance implementing state Senate legislation, replacing a prior interim ordinance
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for California Cigar
Revocation of business license and tobacco retailer permit for Hayes Smoke Shop
Authorization for the Public Works Director to submit a One Bay Area Grant application
Approval of consultant service agreements

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — May 20, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council considered a resolution declaring the city's intent to identify properties designated for a special assessment or district program. The Council also considered setting a public hearing for June 17, 2026, where residents could raise protests before the city finalizes its decision.
keyTopics: Resolution declaring intent to identify designated properties
Scheduling of June 17, 2026 public hearing
Process for residents to file protests
Steps toward final approval of the property designation

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — August 18, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council took up a routine August agenda covering financial reporting, contract approvals, and code updates, along with choosing representatives for an upcoming statewide cities conference. The council also considered whether to continue or move forward with a public hearing on an appeal, and reviewed a second amendment to an existing town agreement.
keyTopics: Approval of August 4, 2026 council meeting minutes
Monthly financial and investment report for June 2026, plus accounts payable and payroll reports
New professional services agreement and a second amendment to an existing town agreement
Selection of a voting delegate and alternate for the League of California Cities Annual Conference
An omnibus ordinance making minor updates to the Town Code, and a decision on whether to continue or hear a pending appeal

san-jose.title: San José City Council — August 18, 2026
san-jose.summary: The San José City Council considered airport lighting upgrades at San José Mineta International Airport, contract amendments for construction management on the regional wastewater treatment plant's improvement program, and continued participation in the Northern California Regional Intelligence Center. The council also looked at joining a coalition focused on making city facilities more resilient and preparing for state climate bond funding, plus a proposed update to the city's list of protected heritage trees.
keyTopics: Airside lighting replacement project at the San José airport
Contract amendments for construction management on the wastewater treatment plant's capital improvement program
Participation in the Northern California Regional Intelligence Center
Joining the Resilient Facilities Coalition and preparing for Proposition 4 climate bond funding
Updates to the city's Heritage Tree List

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee — August 17, 2026
mountain-view.summary: Mountain View's Youth Advisory Committee met to discuss plans for the Summer Movie Nights program and to review the committee's overall purpose, including electing members to leadership positions. The meeting also included time for public comments and committee members to share updates from other city boards and commissions.
keyTopics: Public comments from residents
Planning updates for Summer Movie Nights
Discussion of the Youth Advisory Committee's role and purpose
Election of committee leadership roles (such as chair and vice chair)
Committee member reports on other city boards and commissions

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — August 11, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council held a special study session to consider raising the city's requirements for affordable ('below market rate') housing units in new residential developments, as well as updating the fees developers can pay instead of building those units. The council then moved into its regular 7 P.M. meeting, opening with the flag salute.
keyTopics: Proposed increase to inclusionary housing requirements for new rental developments
Proposed increase to inclusionary housing requirements for new ownership housing
Updating in-lieu fees developers pay instead of building affordable units
Council Priority Project CDD 23-01 on below market rate housing policy
Start of the regular 7 P.M. City Council meeting

cupertino.title: Cupertino Teen Commission — August 12, 2026
cupertino.summary: Cupertino's Teen Commission met to discuss plans for a Bike Fest event and reviewed the Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program. The Commission also heard from Next Vision AI, a youth-led organization, and approved minutes from their June 10 meeting. Time was also set aside for public comments on topics not otherwise on the agenda.
keyTopics: Bike Fest event planning
Juvenile Traffic Diversion Program
Presentation from youth-led group Next Vision AI
Approval of June 10, 2026 meeting minutes
Open public comment period

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 18, 2026
santa-clara.summary: This Santa Clara City Council meeting notice covered mainly procedural details, including that Councilmember Chahal participated remotely from India and information on how residents could join the meeting or submit comments. No specific policy items were detailed in the available agenda information.
keyTopics: Councilmember Chahal's remote participation from Panchkula, India
Hybrid meeting format allowing in-person and remote attendance
Instructions for joining via Zoom or phone
Process for submitting written public comment before the meeting

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — August 3, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered a resolution to place a business tax modernization measure on the ballot, which would shift the city from its current business tax structure to a gross receipts tax model. The proposal was framed around making taxes more closely tied to actual business revenue, protecting small businesses (with about 85% of Milpitas businesses potentially seeing lower or unchanged taxes), and keeping the city competitive with other cities' tax rates.
keyTopics: Resolution to submit a business tax modernization measure to voters
Shift from current business tax structure to a tiered gross receipts tax
Protections and impact for small businesses making up ~85% of local businesses
Comparison of Milpitas's revenue per resident/business against regional competitors
Simplifying tax administration and adapting the tax code for newer business types like tech and gig economy work

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Architectural Review Board — August 6, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Architectural Review Board considered staff recommendations on process and design standards for Tier 2 and Tier 3 wireless communication facilities located in the public right-of-way, such as utility poles and streetlights used for cell equipment. The item was classified as 'Not a Project' under CEQA, meaning it fell outside environmental review requirements entirely.
keyTopics: Design standards for wireless equipment installed in the public right-of-way
Differences between Tier 2 and Tier 3 wireless facility classifications
Review process for approving future wireless installations
Staff presentation outlining recommended criteria for board consideration
CEQA determination that the item is not a project
